# Token-Block Discipline (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.6.0` — GHI #764: adds § Binding Sub-Invariant 7 (the exchange record carries an observation report). The record is two things by operator canon — the fact of block vacation AND an observation report of what happened during possession — and only the first half was implemented: the completion writer had three content inlets for seven sections, so four sections emitted boilerplate byte-identical across all 33 records on disk, and those four are the observation report's own subject matter. The implementation summary was also filed under `## Pending Work / Open Loops`, a prospective heading for retrospective content. Inlets are OPTIONAL and sourced from the brief, so GHI #619's input-free floor is unchanged. Prior `0.5.0` — GHI #763: the token block's register entry is an **exchange record**, named and stored as one. It lived in `.gzkit/handoffs/` under session-handoff identifiers, so system membership had to be *inferred* from a shared word, path, and directory rather than read from a discriminator — and was inferred wrongly twice in one session. Records now live in `.gzkit/locks/exchange/` (location types membership), the writers/finder are `exchange`-named in `gzkit.exchange_records`, and `--lock-handoff-coupling` survives as a deprecated alias of `--lock-exchange-coupling`. § Sub-Invariant 5's predicate is now **default-deny**: it admits only the shape an exchange writer emits, so a document kind nobody admitted is refused without having to be enumerated first. The ledger payload key `handoff_path` is FROZEN on the wire — 204 append-only events carry it. Prior `0.4.0` — GHI #756: § Binding Sub-Invariant 5 now names `mode: CHECKPOINT` as a third disqualifier alongside `abandoned: true`. `mode` was `Literal["CREATE", "RESUME"]` and `find_exchange_for_release` never read it, so once the mid-flight bookmark mode existed, a bookmark postdating the claim would have satisfied the release precondition — a token surrendered on the evidence of a session that never departed. The predicate now skips checkpoints at the live gate and `gz validate --lock-exchange-coupling` backstops it on ledger replay. Prior `0.3.1` — diet pass (operator ruling 2026-08-02): lifted § Vocabulary, § Cross-Links, and § Audit Path to `docs/governance/token-block-doctrine.md` (correcting the retired "5:1 governance ratio" citation in transit); binding sub-invariants unchanged. Prior `0.3.0` — added § Binding Sub-Invariant 6 (completion surrender is mechanical): `gz obpi complete` (and the `gz obpi pipeline` sync stage that invokes it) writes the register-entry handoff and releases any held lock automatically (GHI #619), so the token's exit edge no longer requires an operator-authored handoff or a manual `gz obpi lock release`. This does NOT relax Sub-Invariant 5 — completion produces the register entry mechanically rather than demanding the operator author one; the fail-closed manual release path is unchanged for mid-traversal surrender. Prior `0.2.0` — Sub-Invariant 2 minimum-information channels are now named per-field: items 1/2/4 are frontmatter keys, item 3 is the `## Decisions Made` body section. Resolves the rule↔validator↔producer drift where the prose said "frontmatter or body" but both `gz validate --lock-exchange-coupling` and the machine-generated reaping handoff already use frontmatter. Prior `0.1.1` — trimmed railway-history pedagogy while preserving all lock-release and handoff invariants.

## Doctrine Foundation

**A token cannot be surrendered without a register entry.** Memory is not evidence; lock release is coupled to a handoff document or an explicit abandoned/reaped handoff path.

> See [`docs/governance/token-block-doctrine.md`](../../docs/governance/token-block-doctrine.md) for railway-history lineage, vocabulary mapping, and rationale.

## Binding Sub-Invariant 1: Auditable Abandon Categories

**Rule:** `obpi_lock_release_cmd` and `lock_manager.release_lock()` MUST accept an optional `--abandon <category>:<reason>` flag. When provided, the flag records a degenerate exchange record with `abandoned: true` frontmatter and the category+reason text. When omitted, release requires an existing register entry (§ Binding Sub-Invariant 5).

**Category Enum (Base):** The base enum of abandon reasons is CLOSED. New categories require ADR-backed rationale and a checklist item in the next maintenance ADR. Current base:

- `network_loss` — session network interruption; agent unable to gracefully suspend and create register entry
- `external_blocker` — external service/dependency failure blocking normal completion; agent choosing to abandon rather than retry
- `wrong_obpi_claimed` — agent claimed a lock intended for a different OBPI; discovered in release window
- `tool_failure` — gzkit toolchain failure (crash, corruption, unrecoverable state); operator intervention required

**Extension Protocol:** `--abandon <category>:<reason>` where category MUST be in the base enum above or a registered extension (by name in a published ADR). Unregistered categories are rejected (fail-closed) at CLI parsing time. Reason text is free-form within the chosen category.

**Anti-pattern:** Free-text-only abandonment (e.g., `--abandon "session timeout"`) is prohibited. Every abandon must declare a category to enable audit-driven categorization of failure modes.

## Binding Sub-Invariant 2: Register-Entry Minimum-Information Rule

**Rule:** A register entry (handoff document) is structurally valid only if it carries ALL of the following. The structured channel is canonical, named per-field: items 1, 2, and 4 are **frontmatter keys**; item 3 is the **`## Decisions Made` body section**. This is the single channel `gz validate --lock-exchange-coupling` reads and the one `lock_manager._write_reaping_exchange` already stamps — free-body prose for items 1/2/4 does NOT satisfy the validator.

1. **Last lock-event timestamp** — frontmatter key `last_lock_event_timestamp`: the timestamp of the matching `obpi_lock_claimed` event (from ledger replay) that this handoff concludes. Enables detector to verify: "this handoff matches this lock claim, no lock-release event exists between them."

2. **Last commit SHA** — frontmatter key `last_commit_sha`: the HEAD commit SHA at the time of handoff creation. Enables detector to trace work context back to git state.

3. **Named decision context** — a `## Decisions Made` body section: a one-paragraph prose statement of the work decision(s) made during this traversal: "decided to defer X," "blocked by Y," "completed Z," "transferred to agent-Q." Not a transcript; a semantic summary of the traversal's purpose and outcome.

4. **Branch state** — frontmatter key `branch`: the branch name (e.g. `main`). Enables detector to verify: "handoff-time branch state matches session-start branch state or explains drift."

**Validator Rule (OBPI-0.0.41-04):** Entries lacking any of these four fields MUST fail the `gz validate --lock-exchange-coupling` validator (exit 3, fail-closed). Structurally-valid-but-semantically-empty handoffs (e.g., `title: "Handoff"` + no content) are blocked.

> See [`docs/governance/token-block-doctrine.md`](../../docs/governance/token-block-doctrine.md) for the register-entry rationale.

## Binding Sub-Invariant 3: Reaping Register-Entry Rule

**Rule:** When `lock_manager.reap_expired_locks()` is invoked (by any agent at the start of a new session), a lock found to be expired triggers this sequence:

1. Agent B discovers lock held by Agent A, last claim-event timestamp > TTL-ago (per § Binding Sub-Invariant 4).
2. Agent B MUST create a degenerate exchange record with:
   - Frontmatter: `abandoned: true`, `category: reaping`, `abandoned_by: <agent-id>`, `abandoned_at: <ISO-timestamp>`, `previous_agent: <agent-id-from-claim-event>`
   - Body: statement of the reason for reap (e.g., "TTL 24h exceeded; last activity 2026-05-09 14:22:00Z")
   - Last known state snapshot: commit SHA and branch state from the claim event, if available
3. Agent B invokes lock-release via `obpi_lock_release_cmd --abandon reaping:<reason>` with the degenerate handoff in place. Release succeeds only if the degenerate handoff exists.
4. Ledger records `obpi_lock_released_event` with `handoff_path` pointing to the `abandoned_by_reaper` register entry.

**Anti-pattern:** Reaping without a register entry (i.e., claiming reaping is "automatic" and doesn't require handoff) violates the token-block invariant. Every lock surrender — ordinary or reaping — must be paired with a register entry.

## Binding Sub-Invariant 4: TTL Canon and Reaping Discipline

**Rule:** Lock expiration and reaping are time-bound with the following parameters:

### Default TTL Value

- **Default TTL:** 24 hours (86400 seconds)

### Escalation Policy (Warn-Then-Reap)

- **Warn threshold:** At 12 hours (50% TTL), the SessionStart hook logs a WARNING to console and ledger: "OBPI lock held by <agent> for >12h; consider `gz-session-handoff` skill to create register entry and release."
- **Reap threshold:** At 24 hours (100% TTL), the next SessionStart hook invokes `lock_manager.reap_expired_locks()` automatically, records the `abandoned_by_reaper` register entry, and emits the reaping ledger event.
- **Post-reap holdover:** A reaped lock can be re-claimed by the same or a different agent. The ledger trail (abandoned_by_reaper + new claim) is the audit evidence.

### Reaping Authorization Rule

- **Who may reap:** Any agent at the start of a new session (SessionStart hook) has implicit authorization to reap expired locks.
- **Operator override:** An operator may invoke `lock_manager.reap_expired_locks(force=True)` explicitly (via `gz` CLI or script) to reap locks before TTL expiration. Requires explicit `--force` flag and triggers the degenerate-handoff + release sequence immediately.

### Reaping-Attestation Requirement (Mirror of Release Rule)

**Critical:** The reaping agent MUST produce the `abandoned_by_reaper` degenerate register entry BEFORE `lock_manager.release_lock()` succeeds. The release call fails-closed if the handoff does not exist. This mirrors the § Binding Sub-Invariant 5 rule for ordinary release: token surrender always requires a register entry. Reaping is not an exception; it is the same rule applied to degenerate circumstances.

**Attestation Language:** When OBPI-0.0.41-03 implements this rule, the reaping agent's ledger entry MUST include: `"Reaped lock for OBPI-<id> (agent: <A>, TTL exceeded at <timestamp>); created abandoned_by_reaper register entry at <path> before release."` The register entry path is proof the handoff was created; the ledger entry is the agent's attestation that it was created before the reap.

## Binding Sub-Invariant 5: Release Fail-Closed Precondition

**Rule:** `obpi_lock_release_cmd` and `lock_manager.release_lock()` refuse to release a lock UNLESS one of the following is true:

1. A handoff document exists on-disk whose:
   - Frontmatter timestamp (creation time) is later than the matching `obpi_lock_claimed` event timestamp, AND
   - Frontmatter does NOT contain `abandoned: true`, AND
   - Frontmatter `mode` IS `CREATE` — the default-DENY admit condition, which refuses
     `CHECKPOINT` (GHI #756), `RESUME`, and any mode invented later (GHI #763), AND
   - Document contains all four minimum-information fields (§ Binding Sub-Invariant 2)

- **Binding:** a `CHECKPOINT` handoff never satisfies token surrender.

**Why `CHECKPOINT` is excluded.** A checkpoint is a mid-flight bookmark: the session writes it *without departing*, so it records a pause, never a surrender. Accepting one here would let a bookmark discharge a token release the session never performed — the register entry would exist while the token was still held, which is precisely the state this sub-invariant refuses.

**The predicate is default-DENY (GHI #763).** `is_exchange_register_entry` admits a document only when it carries the shape an exchange writer actually emits — `mode: CREATE` and not `abandoned` — so `CHECKPOINT`, `RESUME`, and any mode invented later are refused without being enumerated. This inverts the earlier blocklist, which admitted by default and subtracted known-bad shapes one reactive commit at a time (`abandoned`, then `CHECKPOINT` under GHI #756); each exclusion could only be written *after* the harm it prevented. Location is the first fence — session documents no longer enter `.gzkit/locks/exchange/` at all — and this predicate is the second. `gz validate --lock-exchange-coupling` remains the ledger-replay backstop for a release whose `handoff_path` was resolved by any other route, and for historical events still citing `.gzkit/handoffs/`.

2. OR the caller provides `--abandon <category>:<reason>` flag, which triggers creation of a degenerate handoff (§ Binding Sub-Invariant 1 and 3) before release.

**Staging:** OBPI-0.0.41-02 implements this as a warning-only precondition ("you're releasing without a register entry; this will become fail-closed in 0.0.41-03"). OBPI-0.0.41-03 flips to fail-closed enforcement.

**Validator Enforcement (OBPI-0.0.41-04):** The `gz validate --lock-exchange-coupling` validator replays the ledger, checks every `obpi_lock_released` event, and fails-closes if any event lacks a valid `handoff_path` reference or the referenced handoff violates the minimum-information rule.

## Binding Sub-Invariant 6: Completion Surrender Is Mechanical

**Rule:** OBPI completion (`gz obpi complete`, and the `gz obpi pipeline` sync stage that calls it) is the token-block **exit edge**: on success it writes a full (non-abandoned) completion handoff as the register entry (§ Sub-Invariant 2 minimum-information fields, auto-drafted from completion evidence) and — if a lock is held — deletes it and emits `obpi_lock_released` citing that `handoff_path`. Surrender is mechanical: no operator prompt, no manual `gz obpi lock release`. The handoff is written BEFORE the delete (fail-safe: if it cannot be written the lock is left for TTL reaping, § Sub-Invariant 4), and the surrender runs AFTER completion's all-or-nothing transaction commits. This does NOT relax § Sub-Invariant 5 — completion produces the register entry mechanically; the fail-closed manual path remains for mid-traversal surrender. (GHI #619.)

## Binding Sub-Invariant 7: The Exchange Record Carries an Observation Report

**Rule:** A completion exchange record MUST carry, in addition to the fact of surrender, an **observation report of the traversal** — what was learned about the block, the residual left for the next occupant, and the artifacts produced. Operator canon, verbatim (2026-08-06, `invariant` tier): *"exchange (noting block vacation and an observation report of what happened)"*.

**Section contract.** Each content kind lands in the section whose tense it matches:

| Section | Content kind | Inlet |
|---|---|---|
| Current State Summary | the surrender fact + what the traversal DID (retrospective) | `implementation_summary` |
| Important Context | what the traversal LEARNED about the block | `observation` |
| Decisions Made | the operator's verbatim Gate-5 attestation | `attestation_text` |
| Immediate Next Steps | the residual left for the next occupant | `residual` |
| Pending Work / Open Loops | open loops at surrender (prospective) | `open_loops` |
| Verification Checklist | the proof the traversal produced | `key_proof` |
| Evidence / Artifacts | artifacts the traversal actually produced | `artifacts` |

**The inlets are OPTIONAL and this is binding, not incidental.** GHI #619 made surrender mechanical because locks were being stranded whenever nobody authored a record. Requiring any inlet would re-create exactly that friction, so the boilerplate fallback remains a valid floor — it simply stops being the normal path. `gz obpi complete` sources `observation` from the brief's `### Value Narrative` and `open_loops` from its `## Tracked Defects`, which is where the completing agent already wrote the observation report; the usual path therefore needs no new operator input.

**Anti-pattern:** placing content in the section it fits rather than the section it belongs to. The implementation summary is retrospective and filing it under `## Pending Work / Open Loops` — as the writer did for all 33 records before GHI #764 — describes finished work as pending. A section that emits byte-identical text across every record is not a low-value section; it is a section with no channel.
